title: Integration linter tests invoke Windows Store Python alias instead of repository interpreter
symptom: zig build test-integration fails TC-TNT-02-03 and TC-TNT-02-04. Both tests spawn tools/lint_migration_schema.py with argv[0] == "python"; on Windows that can resolve to the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias stub, which prints 'Python was not found; run without arguments to install from the Microsoft Store...' and exits 49. The tests observe exit 49 instead of the linter's real exit codes 1 and 0.
reproduction: On Windows with a WindowsApps python.exe alias on PATH: C:/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps/python.exe tools/lint_migration_schema.py <file> -> 'Python was not found...' exit 49. Confirmed on this machine 2026-08-06.
root_cause_analysis: Interpreter selection is by bare name only. 'python' has three PATH resolutions on this machine (Programs/Python312 real, WindowsApps alias stub, AppData/Local/Python/bin shim). Which one wins depends on the PATH the spawning process inherits, which differs between an interactive shell and a zig-build-spawned test binary -- so name-based selection is non-deterministic. ISS-0138 (GH #440) fixed the sibling 'python3' case in build.zig by switching to 'python', but 'python' carries the same WindowsApps alias, and these two call sites live in a test binary rather than build.zig, so that fix does not cover them.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests resolve the repository-selected Python interpreter deterministically on Windows and non-Windows hosts
TC-TNT-02-03 observes expected linter rejection exit 1
TC-TNT-02-04 observes expected linter acceptance exit 0
Full zig build test-integration no longer contains 'Python was not found'
